# Open Context Engine

> Local-first code retrieval and a coding agent that grounds AI in your real codebase. Hybrid semantic + keyword search, an evidence rail that shows what the agent knew, MCP-native, MIT core. One command: `npm install -g @dhaxor/open-context`.

Open Context Engine (OCE) indexes a codebase into a local SQLite store with AST-aware chunking (13 languages), hybrid retrieval (dense vectors fused with BM25), and serves it to any AI agent over the Model Context Protocol — with a fully local mode (in-process MiniLM embeddings, zero API keys) and an audit log that makes every agent run verifiable.

## Pages

- [Home](https://opencontextengine.com/): product overview — hybrid retrieval, evidence rail, local mode, team index sync.
- [Guides](https://opencontextengine.com/guides): index of all field guides — agentic workflows, code RAG, MCP, semantic search, fine-tuning tradeoffs, context engineering.
- [Agentic workflows](https://opencontextengine.com/agentic-workflow): what an agentic workflow is, why code retrieval is the bottleneck, and how OCE grounds agents like Claude Code and Cursor.
- [MCP server for code search](https://opencontextengine.com/mcp-server): connect Claude Code (`claude mcp add oce -- oce mcp`) or Cursor (`oce mcp --http`) to hybrid code search, symbol lookups, repo maps, and file tools over the Model Context Protocol.
- [Code RAG](https://opencontextengine.com/code-rag): what retrieval-augmented generation over source code is, why naive line-chunked vector search fails on real repos, and how to run AST-aware, measured code RAG locally.
- [Semantic code search](https://opencontextengine.com/semantic-code-search): finding code by meaning — where grep and pure vector search each fail, and how hybrid retrieval covers both, measured with recall@k.
- [RAG vs fine-tuning for code](https://opencontextengine.com/rag-vs-fine-tuning): retrieval keeps codebase answers current, grounded, and citable; fine-tuning shapes style. Why code questions usually want RAG.
- [Context engineering](https://opencontextengine.com/context-engineering): the four levers of what an agent sees — retrieval, structure, budget, verification — and OCE's evidence rail.
- [Claude Code setup](https://opencontextengine.com/claude-code): three commands to ground Claude Code in your codebase — `npm i -g @dhaxor/open-context`, `oce index`, `claude mcp add oce -- oce mcp` — with the tools Claude gets and privacy notes.
- [Comparison](https://opencontextengine.com/comparison): OCE vs Cursor vs Copilot vs grep — what each indexes, retrieval tradeoffs, and when a dedicated engine earns its keep.
- [Changelog](https://opencontextengine.com/changelog): every release and what shipped.
- [Docs](https://opencontextengine.com/docs): task-based guides — MCP setup for Claude Code and Cursor, search modes, team index sync, license activation, troubleshooting.
- [Benchmarks](https://opencontextengine.com/benchmarks): measured recall@10 / MRR / nDCG on committed gold sets (this repo, Flask 3.1.2, gin v1.10.0) in keyword-only and hybrid modes, generated from the eval harness's own reports.
- [Pricing](https://opencontextengine.com/pricing): MIT core free forever; Team $25/seat/month for shared indexes and policy locks; offline-verifiable Ed25519 licenses.

## Key facts

- Install: `npm install -g @dhaxor/open-context` (Node 22+).
- MCP: `claude mcp add oce -- oce mcp`, or `oce mcp --http --port 8940 --auth-token <token>` for HTTP clients.
- Works offline: local MiniLM embeddings in-process; keyword-only BM25 as the degradation path.
- Quality is measured, not claimed: committed gold sets and CI baselines; benchmarks page is generated from the eval harness's reports.
- License: MIT core; Team/Enterprise features gate on offline-verifiable license tokens.
- Source: https://github.com/Dhaxor/open-context-engine
